PASS on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/robots/ut-austin-robin__oopsieverse --backend fake (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by stays null. No hardware run, no upstream run and no pip install was made; the clone at a739f99e94f32c3229ae6932299e2e0e8c065480 was read only and stays unmodified. The card's family-config GymnasiumDriver shape fits the confirmed entry symbol oopsiebench.envs.robocasa.close_drawer:DamageableCloseDrawer (oopsiebench/envs/robocasa/close_drawer.py:152); the other four card entry symbols were also found at their cited lines, so there is no DEVIATION FROM THE CARD. The card's mock_strategy.preferred is upstream-sim, but RoboCasa, Robosuite, MuJoCo and gymnasium are not installed where the gate runs and package code never imports or runs the clone; the fake backend is therefore the package's own pure Python stand-in (fake.py), not the upstream environment. The fake models the drawer door state in [0.95, 1.0], the reward 10*(1-mean door state), the 0.05 success threshold, the (observation, info) reset and (observation, reward, done, info) step shapes, and the 23-value robot0_proprio plus a one-value health observation. NOT COVERED: the real RoboCasa/Robosuite/MuJoCo physics (contacts, friction, actuators, sensors, noise), cameras, depth, segmentation and rendering; the real observation keys and the real health-vector length (the number of tracked links is not stated in the clone); the full PandaOmron composite-controller action vector, which is assembled at run time (scripts/teleop_robocasa.py:838-845) and whose size and bounds are not stated in the clone, so the fake serves an unbounded seven-value Box as placeholder test data and no action Limit is invented; and the gripper-distance half of _check_success (close_drawer.py:138-142). The fake's end-effector gain, door travel, start pose and health damage rate are placeholders, marked in fake.py. The sim backend was not run: the clone registers close_drawer in its own EnvironmentRegistry (oopsiebench/envs/registry.py:65) and not with gymnasium.register, so gymnasium.make('close_drawer') is not provided; a real deployment needs an EnvironmentRegistry factory, which this package does not add. The upstream damageable reset() takes no seed argument (damagesim/robosuite/damageable_env.py:382) and the clone defines no seed setter, so the seeded fidelity claim describes the fake, which re-seeds Python's random generator; a real sim deployment would ignore cap.world.seed.v1 and the reset seed, and the fidelity gaps say so. The driver is simulated R0: the package exposes a simulated world, not hardware, and has no physical effect; the card's risk_floor and every catalogue class it binds are R0, and no operator-required bound exists. Warnings, all expected and none from G4: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge buffers the seed for the next reset and makes no native call); G7.MAYBE_ABSENT x3 for action_space, observation_space and close, which come from the external Kitchen/Gymnasium base that the clone's AST cannot follow; G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE because the unbounded action space declares no limit to probe; and G8.NO_UNIT x4 for seed twice, ticks and action.values, simulator inputs whose catalogue classes carry no unit. There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Only cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no extension ids and no catalogue_requests. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; the digest above is the digest line the last check printed.
